candidate.claim: Lean-derived formal evidence is partial and coverage-dependent; finite-sample selective-risk control with abstention is needed before treating it as a trusted decision signal.

paper.title: Risk-Controlled Lean-as-Judge for Natural-Language Mathematical Reasoning

official_code.reproducibility_note: README states main MATH-500 config, Goedel-Prover ablations, pinned Lean 4.21.0 / Mathlib commit 308445d7, fixed threshold grid/splits/seeds, and separate calibration/evaluation pipeline.

coverage_cliff.MATH_500: proof-winning answer is correct about 96% of the time at high proved coverage but 20% at low proved coverage

sparse_unfaithful_signal.implication: Kernel-checked proof of an autoformalized class does not by itself certify faithfulness to the original natural-language problem.

risk_control_mechanism.action: accept only when predeclared coverage/margin conditions pass; otherwise abstain
risk_control_mechanism.certificate: finite-sample selective-risk bound using either conservative Bonferroni grid search or a dev-then-cal regime
risk_control_mechanism.precondition: threshold grid and target risk/confidence must be fixed before calibration labels are inspected; official README warns that changing split seed after inspection violates the certificate precondition

coverage_driven_feasibility.generic_7B: Bonferroni certificate infeasible / abstains on all 20 bootstrap partitions
coverage_driven_feasibility.prover_specialized_formalizer: about 79% coverage; certificate feasible on 17/20 partitions; accepts about 48% of problems at about 0.98 accepted accuracy
coverage_driven_feasibility.baseline_context: self-consistency alone is already about 91% accurate

reproducibility_surface.offline_analyses: bootstrap partitions, two-regime comparison, coverage-cliff breakdowns, McNemar tests, reliability diagrams, proof-faithfulness classifier and paper-number summary are exposed by scripts

scope_clarifications: CovCal is an answer-selection/judging system over natural-language math candidates, not a proof-search action router. Transfer of its coverage/abstention pattern to continue/branch/retrieve/restart decisions is a hypothesis that needs a direct routing experiment.

The finite-sample certificate applies to accepted formal predictions under the paper's calibration assumptions; it does not certify fallback answers, unresolved candidates, an upstream natural-language theorem statement, or arbitrary out-of-distribution reuse.

High proved coverage is not equivalent to proof correctness plus semantic faithfulness. The paper's manual audit shows a major autoformalization-faithfulness gap, so downstream wording must distinguish kernel validity from correspondence to the source problem.
Accepted accuracy around 0.98 occurs with selective coverage around 48% in the specialized-formalizer feasibility setting. It should not be reported as 98% accuracy over all MATH-500 problems.
The 20 bootstrap partitions characterize certificate feasibility/stability in the paper's resampling protocol; they are not 20 independent benchmark replications.

The official repo exposes pinned configurations but gitignored model outputs/caches; this audit verifies the public method/config surface and headline paper values, not an independent numerical reproduction.
confidence: high for headline paper values, certificate design and official reproducibility configuration; medium only for transfer to proof-search routing
unresolved: Direct Lean proof-search router using coverage-aware abstention/selective-risk control for actions such as continue, repair, branch, reretrieve and restart.
Distribution-shift robustness of the calibrated acceptance rule across theorem families, autoformalizers and Lean/mathlib versions.
Joint calibration that accounts for semantic autoformalization faithfulness as a first-class uncertainty source rather than only formal trace coverage.
downstream_instruction: Retain C33 as strong direct evidence that partial Lean evidence requires explicit coverage and abstention before trusted answer selection. Do not present CovCal as a demonstrated proof-search router, and never collapse kernel proof validity into semantic faithfulness of the autoformalized natural-language claim.
